# Helper functions

This module provides utility functions for the diffusion package. Rather than
maintaining one monolithic file, we build `helpers.js` from several small,
named pieces. Each piece is explained in prose immediately before or after
the code, and Entangled weaves them back together into a single file when
you run `entangled tangle`.

The overall shape of the file is laid out first, using noweb references
(the `<<...>>` markers) as placeholders for content defined later in this
document.

```{.javascript file=src/helpers.js}
<<helpers-random-generators>>

<<helpers-steady-state>>

<<helpers-grid-conversion>>

<<helpers-grid-difference>>
```

## Generating random sources and sinks

Diffusion simulations often need randomly scattered "sources" (points that
inject material) and "sinks" (points that remove it). Both are built the
same way: for every cell in a `width` × `height` grid, we roll a random
number and compare it against a probability threshold to decide whether
that cell becomes active.

`createRandomSources` returns a flat `Float64Array` where active cells are
marked with `1.0` and inactive cells with `0.0`. Cells are stored in
row-major order, so the linear index for grid position `(i, j)` is
`j * width + i`.

```{.javascript #helpers-random-generators}
export const createRandomSources = (width, height, probability, rng = Math.random) => {
    const sources = new Float64Array(width * height);
    for (let j = 0; j < height; j++) {
        for (let i = 0; i < width; i++) {
            const idx = j * width + i;
            sources[idx] = rng() < probability ? 1.0 : 0.0;
        }
    }
    return sources;
};
```

`createRandomSources` accepts an optional `rng` parameter defaulting to `Math.random`,
which makes them easy to test deterministically by injecting a seeded
random number generator.

## Detecting steady state

Iterative diffusion solvers need to know when to stop: once the grid stops
changing meaningfully between iterations, the simulation has converged.
`checkForSteadyState` compares two successive grids cell by cell and
returns `true` once the largest absolute difference between them drops
below a `tolerance` threshold (default `1e-5`).

```{.javascript #helpers-steady-state}
export const checkForSteadyState = (prev, current, tolerance = 1e-5) => {
    let maxDiff = 0;
    for (let i = 0; i < prev.length; i++) {
        const diff = Math.abs(current[i] - prev[i]);
        if (diff > maxDiff) {
            maxDiff = diff;
        }
    }
    return maxDiff < tolerance;
};
```

Using the maximum difference (rather than, say, an average) is a
conservative choice: it guarantees every single cell has settled, not just
the grid as a whole on average.

## Converting flat grids to 2D matrices

Internally, grids are stored as flat `Float64Array`s for performance, but
plotting libraries like Plotly expect nested arrays (a 2D matrix). 
`convertTo2D` walks the flat array in row-major order and rebuilds it as
an array of rows, undoing the same `j * width + i` indexing scheme used
when the arrays were created.

```{.javascript #helpers-grid-conversion}
// Convert 1D arrays to 2D matrices for Plotly
export const convertTo2D = (array, width, height) => {
    const matrix = [];
    for (let j = 0; j < height; j++) {
        const row = [];
        for (let i = 0; i < width; i++) {
            row.push(array[j * width + i]);
        }
        matrix.push(row);
    }
    return matrix;
};
```

## Comparing two grids

Finally, `calculateDifference` computes a cell-by-cell absolute difference
between two grids of equal size. This is useful for visualizing where two
solutions diverge — for example, comparing a numerical solution against an
analytic one to check accuracy, or comparing two different solver methods
against each other.

```{.javascript #helpers-grid-difference}
// Compute and display difference
export const calculateDifference = (grid1, grid2) => {
    const difference = new Float64Array(grid1.length);
    for (let i = 0; i < grid1.length; i++) {
        difference[i] = Math.abs(grid1[i] - grid2[i]);
    }
    return difference;
};
```
